requirement.title: Identity-based selection
requirement.description: Replace selectedIndex (number) with selectedTarget (string | null) that tracks the tmux target address of the selected session. Selection resolves against the current visible (possibly filtered) session list on each render.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given selectedTarget is "arcforge:1.1" and the visible session list contains arcforge:1.1, when the session list renders, then the arcforge:1.1 row shows the ▸ indicator.
Given selectedTarget is "arcforge:1.1" but arcforge:1.1 is filtered out by search, when the session list renders, then selectedTarget auto-updates to the first visible session's target.
Given the visible session list is empty (all filtered out or no sessions), when the session list renders, then selectedTarget is null.
Given user presses j/k, when navigating the session list, then selectedTarget updates to the next/previous session's target within the visible list.
Given selectedTarget is "workspace:1.1" and workspace:1.1 disappears between polls, when the session list re-renders, then selectedTarget auto-updates to the first visible session.

requirement.title: Search visual improvements
requirement.description: The search bar gets distinct visual styling and feedback to make the search mode clearly identifiable and the results transparent.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given search mode is active with query "arc", when the search bar renders, then it shows an inverse-color (white-on-cyan) bar: "/ arc 2/5" where 2/5 is match count / total.
Given search mode is active, when user presses j/k, then the selection navigates within the filtered results (not blocked).
Given search mode is active with query "arc", when user presses Enter, then search input deactivates (no more typing), filter remains active, j/k and command input resume.
Given search mode is active, when user presses Esc, then search is cancelled: query is cleared, filter removed, full session list restored.
Given search mode activates (user presses /), when the search bar appears, then selectedTarget resets to the first session in the filtered results.

requirement.title: Status dot colors
requirement.description: Status indicator dots in the session list use per-status colors for at-a-glance monitoring from a distance.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a session with status "active", when the session row renders, then the ● dot is rendered in green.
Given a session with status "idle", when the session row renders, then the ○ dot is rendered with dimColor (default dim foreground).
Given a session with status "needs_attention", when the session row renders, then the ⚡ dot is rendered in yellow.
Given a session with status "unknown", when the session row renders, then the ? dot is rendered in dim red.

requirement.title: Selected row background highlight
requirement.description: The currently selected session row gets a subtle background color to make the selection visible at a glance, beyond the ▸ indicator.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given arcforge:1.1 is selected, when the session list renders, then the arcforge:1.1 row has backgroundColor="gray" on its Box container.
Given arcforge:1.1 is selected and workspace:1.1 is not, when the session list renders, then only arcforge:1.1 has the background highlight.

requirement.title: Notification feed urgency colors
requirement.description: Notification events in the feed are colored by type to create a consistent visual language matching the session list status colors.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a notification with message containing "needs input" or "attention", when the notification feed renders, then the notification text is yellow.
Given a notification with message containing "finished" or "completed", when the notification feed renders, then the notification text is green.
Given a notification with message containing "session ended" or "killed", when the notification feed renders, then the notification text is dim red.
Given a notification with an unrecognized message type, when the notification feed renders, then the notification text uses default dimColor.
